state_meaning: chain.py is complete, pushable Chains wiring with real adapter calls. Every remaining null is a cloud/account/evidence value that only a live Baseten deployment or a frozen protocol artifact can supply, and each carries a resolved_by naming the exact command or step that fills it.
purpose: Required cloud evidence and immutable inputs before the PLUMB Chains topology may execute scored rollout work. Local cluster diagnostics are recorded separately and do not configure or qualify a Baseten deployment.
prepush_requirement: python deploy/baseten/stage_packages.py  (fills deploy/_chain_packages/ with the plumb package, declared as DockerImage.external_package_dirs)

notes: chains.RemoteConfig in 0.18.30 has no autoscaling field: the only min_replica occurrence in the installed SDK is a docstring. Replica and concurrency-target settings are applied post-push through the management API, which is the side plumb/platform.py:598 already reads back.

truss_chains.framework reads endpoint signatures with inspect.signature() and no eval_str, and _validate_io_type rejects string annotations, so chain.py deliberately omits `from __future__ import annotations`.
utils.make_abs_path_here must be called inline at module level; chain.py does that for every requirements path.
truss renders build_commands after the requirements install, which is why MiniVLA's flash-attn source build can rely on torch 2.2.0 already being present.

DockerImage takes `requirements_file` on modern truss and the deprecated alias `pip_requirements_file` on older ones. chain.py feature-detects the field name from DockerImage.model_fields, so it is pushable on either and emits no deprecation warning on 0.18.30.

validated.method: Installed truss==0.18.30 in a throwaway venv, imported deploy/baseten/chain.py, and ran truss_chains.framework.raise_validation_errors().
validated.result: no validation errors collected; all nine Chainlets constructed, the entrypoint resolved eight dependencies each with retries=0, and both endpoints validated as async with pydantic I/O
validated.does_not_establish: This validates the SDK surface and the module's own definitions. It is NOT a push, NOT an image build, and NOT evidence about GPU behaviour, capacity, latency, or cost.
validated.reproduce: python3 -m venv /tmp/plumb-truss && /tmp/plumb-truss/bin/pip install 'truss==0.18.30' && /tmp/plumb-truss/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_chain.py -k framework_validator -v

cluster_runtime_evidence.why_it_does_not_transfer: HANDOFF.md pins Alliance/ComputeCanada local wheel builds (torch 2.6.0+computecanada, tokenizers 0.19.1+computecanada, transformers 5.17.0+computecanada). Those version strings do not exist on PyPI, so every Baseten image installs a different binary build of the same upstream version. Kernels, CUDA minor versions, attention backends, and allocator behaviour all differ, so the recorded timings, GPU peaks, and cold-load seconds are not evidence about any image defined here (AGENT-BUILD-SPEC.md 12).
does_not_establish: Baseten container digests, deployed images, routes, or serializers
Baseten account capacity, active replicas, pricing, or cost
scenario parity, policy/world feedback fidelity, human calibration, or Gates A-F

async_submission.internal_rpc_rule: Only the Chain entrypoint uses the external async queue. Internal Chainlet calls are awaited RPCs created by chains.depends(..., retries=0) and must never re-enter the queue.
async_submission.queue_status_reason: The model-scoped async_queue_status route is not evidence of a Chain route. Until an account-tested exact route exists, plumb.platform reports the platform queue as unavailable rather than guessing.
async_submission.queue_status_route_resolved_by: After the push, call the candidate Chain queue route with the deployment's API key, save the raw response body as the evidence artifact, then construct plumb.platform.VerifiedChainQueueRoute(url=..., evidence_uri=<saved response URI>, verified_at=<ISO-8601 with offset>). See DEPLOY.md step 8.

assets.purpose: Avoid paying the recorded 167.683719175 s Cosmos cold load on every replica, which would be fatal to a 60-second burst. The residual cold-start cost on THIS image is unmeasured.
assets.residual_cold_start_seconds_resolved_by: Time a scale-from-zero replica start on Baseten separately from steady-state inference, per spec 7's requirement to keep the live 1-to-100 scale-up experiment separately timed.
assets.cached_selection_rule: Only the SELECTED arm is cached. Mounting the unused sibling would add its multi-gigabyte download to every container start for no benefit, and container-start time is exactly what the 60-second burst cannot afford. RolloutController.loop_contract: For each control boundary: policy -> compile actions (plumb.adapters.bridge.BridgeToCosmosCompiler on CPU) -> world -> accumulate frames, dropping the echoed conditioning frame -> persist a SegmentResult; after the horizon: validity, then judge.
RolloutController.prefix_rule: The loop advances by the adapter's certified executed prefix. When certified_execute_prefix is null the episode returns blocked. It never assumes five chunks, never truncates, and never pads; a shorter terminal prefix requires demonstrated prefix invariance or an exact supported terminal length.
RolloutController.retries: chains.depends(..., retries=0) for every dependency. A transport retry creates an attempt, not a new statistical episode, and attempt accounting belongs to the application ledger.
RolloutController.frame_transport: PNG base64 with separate png_sha256 and pixels_sha256, because HANDOFF.md records that schema-v1 labelled pixel hashes ambiguously. Digests are verified on every decode; a mismatch is an explicit failure.
RolloutController.segment_events: RolloutResult.segments carries hash-bound per-segment records so the control plane can emit segment_completed events and persist artifacts before advancing.

telemetry_and_economics.desired_or_starting_replicas_resolved_by: Query the account's supported metrics export for desired/starting replica series. If the account does not expose it, display unavailable; never derive it from max_replica.
telemetry_and_economics.compute_seconds_source: RolloutResult.gpu_seconds, an instrumented per-stage measure (stage wall seconds times declared GPU count)
telemetry_and_economics.allocated_gpu_seconds_resolved_by: The application's resource-allocation ledger, recording every allocation interval from prewarm start through cooldown exactly once. It is a separate ledger from instrumented stage timings and must stay separately labelled.
telemetry_and_economics.pricing_currency_resolved_by: Read the account's instance-type prices via the management API AND confirm currency, billing unit, resource applicability, and tax/egress/storage treatment against the vendor/account contract; then construct plumb.platform.VerifiedPriceBasis(currency=<3-letter uppercase>, unit=<PriceUnit>, evidence_uri=<saved contract or API response URI>, retrieved_at=<ISO-8601 with offset>). See DEPLOY.md step 10.
telemetry_and_economics.pricing_unit_resolved_by: Same step. Do not assume an API field named `price` is already per-hour USD; plumb.platform keeps rate_per_hour unavailable until the unit is evidenced.
telemetry_and_economics.estimated_usd_resolved_by: Only after a VerifiedPriceBasis exists: estimated_usd = sum(resource_rate_per_hour * allocated_resource_hours) + other_charges, over nonoverlapping allocations, reported separately as a marginal execution estimate and a total demonstration-run cost.
telemetry_and_economics.settled_cost_resolved_by: Billing reconciliation after usage posts. Until then every cost result stays qualified as an estimate.
telemetry_and_economics.reason: No currency, billing unit, or resource applicability is assumed from the numeric instance-type price field, and null means unknown, never zero.

performance_target.target: 1,500 episodes in 60 seconds for approximately $11 (operationally <= $11.25 total demonstration-run cost)
performance_target.throughput_preset_reason: AGENT-BUILD-SPEC.md:285 states there is no assumed universal throughput preset. Batch size, concurrency, and replica counts in this file are hypotheses to be re-tuned from measured memory and full-chain throughput.
performance_target.measured_full_chain_throughput_resolved_: Gate A on Baseten: run the deployed payload at increasing batch sizes and replica counts, record GPU memory, per-stage latency, and episodes/second, then re-derive batch_max, predict_concurrency, and max_replica from those measurements.
performance_target.measured_cold_start_seconds_resolved_by: Time the 1-to-100 scale-up as a separately reported measurement; cold starts must not be hidden inside a supposedly instantaneous transition.

qualification.statement: No Chainlet may declare itself qualified. RolloutResult.qualified is hard-coded false: Gates A-D are external reviews recorded in plumb.gates and are never inferred from a call that happened to return.

tests.note: 159 pass in the project venv with truss_chains absent; the 160th runs only in the deploy venv and executes the real truss_chains framework validator. Two AST guards cover the branch under `if CHAINS_RUNTIME_AVAILABLE:` that cannot execute locally: every pydantic construction uses declared fields, and every local call uses declared keywords. Both were verified to fail when the bug they guard is reintroduced.

result_contract.stages: Dict[str, StageResult] -- TERMINAL status per stage name, indexed by stage name by plumb/backends/baseten.py.
result_contract.stage_history: List[StageResult] -- the full ordered record. A rollout makes one policy and one world call per certified executed prefix, so the mapping above keeps only the last of each.
result_contract.progress_score: Rollout-level progress, named to match plumb.rollout.RolloutReport and the reader in plumb/backends/baseten.py. The judge's own report keeps its `progress` field.
result_contract.gpu_seconds: Instrumented per-stage GPU seconds only. allocated_gpu_seconds stays null and no USD is derived.
result_contract.segments: Hash-bound per-segment records so the control plane can emit segment_completed events and persist artifacts before advancing.
result_contract.missing_reason: Composed as stage_<name>_<status> (for example stage_world_blocked), matching the format plumb/backends/baseten.py builds when it has to derive one.
